campaigns.title: Help Hari rescue injured monkeys left to suffer in agony
campaigns.description: “When I see a monkey lying on the roadside, abused by people or bleeding after getting electrocuted, I feel their pain as if it were my own. They scream not just in agony, but in fear that they might be beaten up again,” says Hari Kishan Mangle, founder of Guardian of Angels, an NGO devoted to rescuing and treating injured and abused monkeys.Hari spent everything to set up a rescue and rehabilitation centre equipped to treat animals but his own efforts could take him only this far. He is in urgent need of support to continue providing urgent medical care to monkeys and other animals. Your donation can mean life for an animal. Donate generously.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking.Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).Every life mattersAcross India, monkeys suffer silently — electrocuted on live wires, run over by vehicles, beaten, or trapped. “We find them with broken backs, deep burns, or shattered limbs. Some tremble so much from fear they won’t even touch food,” says Hari Kishan.At Guardian of Angels, every rescue is a race against time. The team rushes to the spot, stabilises the monkey with emergency care, and brings them to the centre for treatment. Trained veterinarians clean wounds, perform surgeries, and nurse them back to health. “Watching a monkey who couldn’t move begin to climb again after weeks of treatment, that’s what keeps us going,” Hari Kishan shares.From fear to freedomMany monkeys that reach Guardian of Angels have endured unimaginable cruelty, chained for years, burned, or beaten for amusement. “When they first arrive, their eyes are full of pain and distrust,” says Hari Kishan. “But with time, care, and love, those same eyes begin to soften. They start to trust again.”Once recovered, the team ensures the monkeys are safely released back, far from the dangers of roads and electric lines. For those who can never return, the centre becomes their permanent home, where they can play, rest, and live without fear.Why your help is urgently neededRescuing and healing an injured monkey takes days of intensive care and resources, from medicines and surgeries to food and shelter.With calls for help increasing every week, Guardian of Angels struggles to meet the growing cost of care. “Every life matters. But sometimes, due to lack of funds, we have to make heartbreaking choices,” says Hari Kishan. “That’s why we’re asking for your support, so no suffering animal is ever left behind.”Your donation will help:Rescue and transport injured and abused monkeysProvide life-saving medical treatment and surgeriesFeed and rehabilitate recovering monkeysExpand and maintain the shelter for long-term residentsBe their guardian, give them hope, healing, and lifeYour contribution helps an injured monkey stand again, eat again, live again. It turns suffering into safety and fear into freedom.Join Guardian of Angels in their mission to rescue, heal, and protect India’s monkeys. Your kindness can save a life today.Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Guardian of Angels Trust in its mission to rescue and rehabilitate injured monkeys.

campaigns.title: Gau Seva – Help Satsang Foundation Gaushalas protect our indigenous cows
campaigns.description: Based on the vision of sustainable living of our founder Sri M, The Satsang Foundation (TSF) established two Gaushalas - one at the Madanapalle Ashram and the other at The Sacred Grove (TSF’s Wellness Centre) in Chowdepalle, Andhra Pradesh. A total of 31 indigenous Gir, Sahiwal, Rathi and Tharkapar cows are cared for in the gaushalas.Gaushala at the Madanapalle AshramThis was carved out of Sri M’s personal garden in September 2019 to create a loving home for 10 Gir and Sahiwal cows.Salient Features:-  Provides fresh milk, buttermilk, and ghee for the in-house community kitchen Madhu Ki Rasoi, which offers Annadaanam all through the year to visitors, volunteers and residents at the Ashram and students and staff of The Satsang Vidyalaya.-   Fuels the kitchen with natural biogas, reducing usage of expensive cooking gas.Gaushala Kshetra within The Sacred GroveThis tranquil Gaushala is Vrindavan incarnate in Chowdepalle. Canopied by Kadamba trees and pulsating with the notes of the flute, the gaushala is home to 21 Gir, Sahiwal, Rathi and Tharkapar cows.Salient features:- Promotes eco-friendly farming practices through calf adoption: Upholds Gau-Paalan (care and nourishment of cows) by placing year-old calves with farmers, encouraging indigenous breed preservation and sustainable agriculture.- Revives traditional process of cold-pressed oil extraction for a healthier lifestyle.- Contributes to ethical animal husbandry by partnering with government semen collection projects, ensuring responsible breeding practices for cows.On an average, the annual maintenance cost for a cow at the Gaushalas amounts to ₹60,000. This covers the full cost of food, shelter, supplies and medical treatment for 1 cow for a whole year. It also takes care of administrative expenses, such as, staff salaries, transportation of supplies, shelter & grazing land maintenance, etc.Sponsorship Options: Adopt 1 cow for a month: ₹5,000Adopt 5 cows for a month: ₹25,000Adopt 10 cows for a month: ₹50,000Adopt 1 cow for a year: ₹60,000Adopt 5 cows for a year: ₹3,00,000Adopt 10 cows for a year: ₹6,00,000Support our this sacred cause and earn blessings!

campaigns.title: URGENT!! People of Assam need urgent help as floods leave lakhs in need. Donate now
campaigns.description: People of Assam need urgent help as floods leave lakhs in need. Donate nowFloodwaters have once again ravaged the beautiful land of Assam, leaving a trail of destruction in its wake. According to the latest reports by the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), over six lakh people have been severely affected by floods across Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, Sivasagar, and other districts. The number of victims of the natural disaster has climbed to over 70, while thousands remain stranded without help. Together, let us rise and make a difference by contributing to our fundraising campaign for the flood victims of Assam.Charaideo is the worst-hit district with nearly 1.9 lakh people affected, followed by Sivasagar (over 1.5 lakh) and Jorhat (around 1.4 lakh). Nestled in the northeastern part of India, Assam has a long-standing history of facing nature's fury. Just last year, the state witnessed a devastating flood that uprooted the lives of countless individuals. This year, the floods have struck again, plunging numerous families into unimaginable chaos and distress. Many have been displaced from their homes, left without shelter, and robbed of their basic necessities.Embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure have also been damaged by flood waters. The urgent need for assistance:In times like these, it is our duty to extend a helping hand to our fellow human beings who are facing the wrath of nature. Your generous donations will directly support our on-ground NGO partners who are tirelessly working to provide immediate relief to the flood-affected people in Assam. The funds raised will be utilised to provide them with essential supplies such as food, clean water, and medical care, bringing hope and solace to their lives during this moment of crisis.The power of your donations:Every rupee contributed to this fundraising campaign will create a ripple effect of positive change in the lives of those who need it the most. Your support will help in:Immediate Relief: Ensuring that the affected families receive immediate assistance in the form of food, clean water, and essential supplies.Medical Care: Providing medical aid to those injured or suffering from waterborne diseases, ensuring their well-being in the aftermath of the disaster.Shelter and Rehabilitation: Assisting in the construction of temporary shelters and facilitating the process of rehabilitation to help affected families rebuild their lives.Here's how your donations can help:a) A food kit comprising essential supplies can be provided for ₹1,255. b) A hygiene kit with essentials for an entire family during floods can be ensured for ₹1,035. c) Our NGO partner can provide temporary shelter for flood-affected families for ₹2,570.Now is the time to unite and show our solidarity with the people of Assam. By donating to our fundraising campaign, you are not just providing immediate relief; you are also offering hope and strength to those who have lost everything. Together, we can make a difference and rebuild the lives of the flood-affected communities in Assam. Join us today and let compassion guide our actions.

campaigns.title: Assam Flood Crisis: The water is gone, but the struggle continues. Help Us Rebuild!
campaigns.description: Imagine watching your home fill with water in less than 15 minutes.When sudden floods struck Upper Assam, water levels surged over 11 feet in minutes. Families were forced onto rooftops through the night, surviving for days on collected rainwater because every local tube well was buried under mud and sewage.Now, the floodwaters have receded, the short-term food packets are gone, and most external relief drives have packed up and left. But for hundreds of families, the real struggle has just begun. They are returning to homes choked with 3 to 5 feet of heavy silt, with no mattresses, no bedsheets, no cookware, no clothes, and contaminated drinking water. Food aid sustained them for a few days, but you cannot rebuild your life on a food packet.At Sunbird Trust, our team operates in these remote regions. We don't pack up when the waters go down. Our field teams have been waded deep into affected villages across Sivasagar, conducting detailed, household-by-household ground assessments alongside local villagers and identified 11 severely affected villages. The need on the ground is immense:Over 1,800 Households need urgent support to clear thick mud, sanitise flooded rooms, and replace destroyed living essentials like bedding, utensils, hygiene items, and dignity support for women.Over 423 Households have had their homes completely flattened and need long-term shelter reconstruction.While our long-term plan is to support these families with housing reconstruction and sustainable livelihood opportunities so they can fully recover, our immediate focus right now is restoring their basic health, safety, and living dignity.Rebuilding an entire state takes time and immense resources. But these families cannot wait months while sleeping on damp, mud-choked floors without basic cookware or clean water. We are raising a ₹25 Lakh Emergency Fund to deliver comprehensive living and hygiene kits directly into the hands of the most vulnerable families.These kits are built based on direct conversations with families on the ground:Health & Sanitisation: Heavy phenyl and bleaching powder to sanitise mud-filled rooms and stop disease outbreaks.Mud Clearance & Shelter: Spades to dig out heavy silt, heavy-duty tarpaulins, ropes, and torches.Living Dignity: Fresh mattresses, pillows, and bedsheets so children and elders don't sleep on damp, contaminated ground.Family Needs: Cooking utensils, dry rations, baby food, and essential clothing sets for women.When the emergency headlines end, that is when flood survivors need us the most. You don't have to fund an entire kit to make a difference. Whether you can give 100, 500, 2,000, or 10,000, every single rupee goes directly to our verified, last-mile ground operations in Sivasagar.The people of Upper Assam have shown incredible resilience through this disaster. Please don't let them fight this battle alone in the mud.Please donate today, share this campaign with your network, and stand with Sunbird Trust as we rebuild lives on the ground.

campaigns.description: Every day, elderly parents are left alone on the streets, at train stations, or even outside temples. Many are sick, struggling with age-related problems, and have no money or family to turn to. Some suffer for weeks or months before anyone notices their pain. The heartbreaking truth? The problem is only getting worse.But there is hope. Our dedicated NGO partners work day and night to rescue these forgotten elders. They provide safe shelter, medical care, nutritious meals, and most importantly—love and respect. Through old age homes across the country, our partners give these seniors a chance to live their remaining years with dignity, comfort, and peace.You can make a difference. Your donation will help our NGO partners:Rescue homeless elders from the streetsProvide shelter, food, and medical careRestore their faith in humanity with kindness and supportNo elder should spend their final years alone and suffering. Your generosity can give them a fresh start. Donate today and help an abandoned senior citizen find safety, care, and hope.

campaigns.title: Therapeutic Community For Victims of Sex Trafficking
campaigns.description:
Commercial sexual exploitation (CSE) is one of the most disparaging crimes crippling India’s social development and economy and threatening the dignity and security of women and children. In this context, the southern states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are no exception. These states continue to constitute the core destination areas for the victimization of trafficked women and children for economic profiteering at the cost of their human rights. Despite the absence of official statistics on CSE in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, civil society organisation estimates suggest that one out of every four victims rescued from CSE is a child and 60 per cent of all rescued children from CSE are HIV positive. Further, 75 per cent of females in the Telugu region between the ages of 15-35 years are found to be engaged in sex work.[1] Reports in the print and digital news media also indicate that sex trafficking of both vulnerable women and children is progressively on the increase. Given the scale of the issue, the government has not placed due attention and priority on the rescue and rehabilitation of CSE victims in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. In addition, there is a lack of systems and capacity to conduct MEL and research, weak and uncoordinated monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) of existing programs and no investment in empirical research to understand gaps and issues. Rehabilitation of trafficking survivors remains the most persistent challenge within the current legislative framework. Rescued victims require specialised support services to recover from and overcome the years of trauma-induced mental health issues, physical atrocities and social stigma attached to being former sex slaves. In the absence of statutory rehabilitation that ensures complete and sustainable reintegration into society, CSE victims, even if removed temporarily from their immediate environment marked by social, economic, sexual, psychological and physical extremities, are highly likely to end up in the same vicious cycle of sex trafficking, either through the nexus of same perpetrators or new agents who are on the lookout for feeding on their aggravated vulnerabilities for the second time around. On-ground organisations lament that CSE victims who only receive piece-meal assistance and support post-rescue remain uncertain about their future prospects in absence of hope for alternate opportunities to sustain themselves and end up going back to sex slavery. The circumstances surrounding this lack of choice with CSE victims are marked by haplessness and isolation due to lack of specialised support services for destigmatizing their identities and acute availability of comprehensive rehabilitation measures. Given the scale of CSE in both Telugu states, the following issues have emerged:There is no comprehensive protection and rehabilitation policy in place for CSE victims, either in the states or at the national level. Nor there are adequate budgetary allocations in the two states. In fact, Andhra Pradesh does not even have a budget line for CSE rehabilitation facilities and services.  Rescue operations for removing victims of CSE from situations of abuse are ill-conceived and ill-executed due to a lack of comprehensive understanding of the crime and tactical expertise and a lack of industry standards for conducting such raids and rescues.Institutional infrastructure (shelter homes/protective and rehabilitative homes/child care institutions) for rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of CSE is insufficient and severely ill-equipped to address their complex needs for recovery and effective, holistic rehabilitation, whose numbers are advancing with each passing year. As per an article published in the Indian Journal of Gender Studies, there is a lack of comprehensive protection services such as psychological counselling from trained counsellors through the Ujjawala and Swadhar schemes. This issue was further exacerbated in 2014 after the bifurcation of the Telugu region between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana 2014, where most rehabilitation homes fell under Telangana’s territory and Andhra Pradesh was left with close to none. At present, both states have 5 shelter homes each, for women.There is a severe gap in meaningful and relevant data to even gain an understanding of the gaps and barriers in the rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of CSE victims. A study suggests that though there is abundant literature on trafficking worldwide as well as in South Asia, we still do need region-specific and locally-contextualised data that will yield theoretical and empirical insights, and lead to relevant policy interventions. 
 Sex trafficking is a multi-dimensional problem especially with regard to its impact on the lives of the victims. The tormenting experiences of being betrayed, sold and exploited by the people around (largely includes pimps, brothel owners and customers) takes a long-term toll on the victims. This traumatic situation combined with sexually transmitted diseases, chronic depression, suicidal tendencies, alcohol and drug addiction complicates the cycle of rehabilitation. Hence, the process of rehabilitation has to be an interlinked chain of psychological healing, vocational empowerment, economically viable and socially acceptable. In order to address the physical, emotional and psychological brokenness of the sex-trafficked victims, Prajwala formulated a holistic, therapeutic approach to support the rehabilitation process. The overall aim is to help the victims to overcome their trauma by providing them with psychological and coping skills and tools required to regain stability to lead a normal life. Therefore, the rehabilitation in Prajwala is a blend of psychological healing, civic empowerment and social identity. The three-pronged stages of rehabilitation spearheaded by Prajwala include:Psychological Rehabilitation: Trauma Care, Counselling, Psychiatric CareEconomic Rehabilitation: Life-Skills, Employability Training, Education/Livelihood programCivic Rehabilitation: Aadhar Card, Bank Account, Interim Relief, CompensationA therapeutic community as a safe shelter has been established that provides holistic rehabilitation and has been instrumental in the social reintegration support of thousands of victims 
 600 victims of sex trafficking will be supported every year

campaigns.title: Adoption of 62 Widow Ladies from Eraiyur village for Daily Support
campaigns.description:
Eraiyur village, (Kanchipuram district, close to Sriperumbudur), is a remote village about 44 km south-west of the city of Chennai. Here, a set of old village ladies are suffering, having no kith and kin or any income from any quarter except owning a small house in the village. Most of them are above 75 years of age and their day to day living is becoming problematic.  These elderly senior citizens can no more cook for themselves due to advanced age and slowly in the 3 years that we have been supporting them, their number has grown and at present, there are 62 such ladies in Eraiyur village who are in need of help and support 
 About 3 years ago, NLCT started supporting 10 widow ladies and has now expanded support to about 62 ladies. NLCT now provides a packet of groceries to each of the 62 elderly ladies every month and also takes care of their medical expenses. Those who cannot cook, hand over these groceries to their neighbours who cook for them along with cooking for their families.Apart from these, in case of any urgent needs, these ladies approach NLCT home for help. This way, their day to day problems are taken care and they are able to handle their lives better.Presently due to meagre corpus NLCT is unable to fulfil the recurring expenses of both 120 residents of NLCT home along with 62 community senior citizens family, however the present cost of each senior citizen's monthly requirement tunes to Rs.2500/- per person. 
 With NLCT supporting them, we are confident that they are living a better life as they don’t have to struggle for their daily needs and don’t have to starve. As they can no more work for themselves for their livelihood, this support is very helpful. NLCT is not in a position to in-house all the 62 senior citizens due to space constraints, but we found a solution by offering to help them with groceries, medicines, medical help/camps, ambulance services etc, so that they can live in their own homes, but get all other support forms NLCT.

campaigns.title: Donate a Sewing Machine to Poor Woman & Tailoring Training
campaigns.description: This project will train 150 poor women and teach them valuable sewing skills. It will also provide each woman with her own treadle sewing machine, allowing her to earn a living from home to support her family.Challenge: To a struggling woman or girl in countries like India, the sewing machine you provide can be the doorway to a better life. You’ll help a single mother, orphaned teen, or widow feel the dignity of providing for herself and her family. In India, more than 50 per cent of women are illiterate. Living in poverty with a limited education greatly obstructs these women from finding quality jobs to support their families. They are often at risk of being trapped in dehumanizing professions (like the sex trade) in order to feed their children. This project will empower poor women in rural villages with valuable sewing skills and a sewing machine so they can earn a respectable living and help their families.Solution:  The women will attend a sewing machine tailoring centre and get 6 months of training, where they will develop their sewing skills and learn about basic business practices. Once a woman graduates from the tailoring program, she will receive her own treadle (foot powered) branded sewing machine. She will be able to start her own tailoring business from home and earn a daily income that can provide food and basic necessities for the whole family.Long-Term Impact: The project will empower 150 women each year with sewing skills and provide them with a sewing machine to start their own self-sustaining tailoring business. These women, who are often poor mothers and widows, will have an opportunity to use their skills to rise out of poverty and work toward a promising future for themselves and their families.#womenempowerment #sewingmachinedonation #donateonline #donatecharity #charitydonation #sponsorfood #fooddonation #donatingmoney #ngodonation #donatengo #girlchilddonation #sponsorsewingmachine #supportpoorpeople #indiahelpaged #donatepoor #giveindadonation #donatefood #givedonation #donategiveindia #givefoundation #giveonline #covid-19 #coronavirus #pandemic #donatecorona #taxexemption #80gdonation #donatingcharity #caronavirusoutbreak #CoronaCombatForce #secondwave #coronasecondwave #poorpeopledonation #bestcharitydonation #donateforpoor #usddonation #moneydonation #tailoringtrainingforwomen #skilltrainingdonation #donatecare #giveindiadonations #globalgiving #CharityforPoor #FeedTheNeedy #MilaapDonation #HelpPoor #donatemoney #onlinedonation #80gtaxexemption

campaigns.title: Help Save Young Girls From Trafficking
campaigns.description: Human trafficking in India is a horrifying crisis. Thousands of victims, primarily women and girl children, are exploited in red-light areas. Over 10,659 cases were reported between 2018-2022, but experts say that these numbers are likely a fraction of the reality due to underreporting, yet they still do expose the magnitude of the crisis. Girls make up 71.4% of missing children in India and a large number of these girls end up at red-light areas. Sex trafficking is particularly gruesome, with girls as young as 12 sold for as little as a few thousand rupees.
